statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56389: GNU Bison accepts %define tool.xsltproc in a grammar file and passes that value to execvp() when it generates an HTML report, so running bison --html on an attacker-supplied grammar runs an arbitrary program with the privileges of the Bison process. Sources: https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/07/CVE-2026-56389/ and the upstream fix https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/bison.git/commit/?id=3169c1e7a2c6acc4c59dfcf8b089896d6881925b, which removes tool.xsltproc from src/print-xml.c and src/reader.c and always runs xsltproc from PATH. No GNU Bison release contains the fix yet; 3.8.2 is the latest release at https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bison/. We read every package built from source bison in the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository: bison 3.8.2-r2 and 3.8.2-r3 for x86_64 and aarch64, and the bison-doc packages of both versions, which hold documentation, examples and manual pages; each package was checked against its index checksum. In all four bison packages, /usr/bin/bison, a dynamically linked program for musl, still contains the string tool.xsltproc, which the fix removes from both places that use it; the same search finds the message %s failed with status %d as a control. So no published build carries the fix. A rebuild that applies the upstream fix is pending, and until it is published every published build is affected.
